newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fore! Australian MPs hit work for a six.
newsitem.headline: Fore! Australian MPs hit work for a six.

text.p: VIP seats for the cricket at Lord's, golf on the world's top courses, tours through France's Bordeaux wine region -- Australia's elected politicians are doing it tough.

Australia's Labor opposition, accusing Prime Minister John Howard of junketeering on a cricket-laden official visit to London, came under fire on Thursday for some of its own members' overseas jaunts.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told parliament that Labor industry spokesman Simon Crean had asked for a hire car for a week in Bordeaux during parliament's winter recess next month, when Canberra temperatures plummet.
And former foreign minister Gareth Evans followed a morning of golf with an afternoon of cricket, along with three other ministers, during an official London visit in 1993, he added.
Labor has criticised Howard, a keen cricketer and monarchist, for indulging himself on his visit to London.

Howard's programme is loaded with three cricket events -- including two sessions of the opening day's play of the second test between Britain and Australia -- a meeting and a lunch with Queen Elizabeth, Australia's head of state, and tea with his conservative idol, former prime minister Margaret Thatcher.
He is also planning a 45-minute meeting with Britain's new Labour prime minister, Tony Blair.
